nonBlockingNotes: Pre-existing, not ours: the harness vitest project's include list has an entry 'layers/core-api/src/routes/__tests__/*-real.integration.test.ts' that matches zero files — inert, and by CLAUDE.md's own rule a scan matching nothing reads as passing forever. Worth its own item.

Pre-existing, NOT ours: a byte-accurate scan of 2,090 source files found two more files containing NUL bytes — layers/core-ui/src/block/block-id.ts (production) and its test layers/core-ui/src/block/__tests__/derive-blocks.test.ts. Same defect class as B2: git shows them as binary, so they are unreviewable in any diff and invisible to plain grep. Untouched by this branch. Its own item.

Dev-environment finding, not ours: `remote-server` reads no .env file — there is no dotenv and no --env-file anywhere in it — so DATABASE_URL cannot be set that way for `npm run dev`. The only levers are the real process environment or .claude/launch.json. Worth knowing before anyone tries to point a dev run at a different database.

Dev-environment finding, not ours: after boot the server reported all four harnesses as 'missing — not installed or not on PATH', which disables onboarding's submit entirely. The binaries were present and on the server's PATH the whole time (verified via its process environment), answer --version in 0.03-0.42s, and running discoverLocalHarnesses directly in the tree reports all four 'ready'. POST /api/harnesses/redetect fixes it in place — so the boot-time discovery snapshot can be stale, and nothing in the UI tells a person to re-detect. Worth its own item: a first-run user would conclude HyperIdle cannot see their CLIs.

Live-run finding to re-test: adding a filesystem whose path does not exist FAILED silently through the Add dialog (no new row appeared, no visible error captured), while the same payload POSTed directly to /api/filesystems returned 201 with state needs_attention. So the server behaves correctly and the dialog does not surface that outcome. Not yet diagnosed.

Corrected diagnosis: remote-server is DESIGNED to have no local harness (empty AdapterPool + createSandboxAdapter('disabled'); agents arrive as remote workers). The Settings page states it: 'Worker mode requires the desktop app.' So NoEligibleHarnessError under `npm run dev` is correct behaviour. Harness DISCOVERY still populates descriptors for display, which is why Settings shows all four 'Authenticated and ready' while no agent can actually run — a genuinely confusing pair of surfaces for a first-run user, worth its own item.

evidence.case: the credential path is HyperIdle's own, proven against REAL GitHub on a real private repository
evidence.why: this machine's global git config already wires gh as a credential helper, so a plain successful clone would prove nothing about this branch
evidence.how: ran git ls-remote against the private repo twice with GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null and GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=/dev/null, i.e. the ambient configuration suppressed
evidence.result: WITHOUT the injected environment: 'fatal: could not read Username for https://github.com' — unreachable. WITH exactly the GIT_CONFIG_COUNT/KEY_0/VALUE_0 credential.<host>.helper = '!gh auth git-credential' that this branch injects per process: returns the private repo's real ref 80ecbef. So authentication rides gh, configured for that one process, with nothing written to the person's git config.
evidence.caveat: the printed exit=0 lines were head's exit status, not git's; the evidence is the error message versus the returned ref
